concepts.def: Weapons of mass destruction — nuclear, biological, chemical
Owning nukes to discourage attack — debated by religions
Use of violence to spread fear for political ends
Refuses to fight on moral or religious grounds
War fought for religious reasons — historically the Crusades
Restoring peace after conflict — e.g. Truth Commissions

walkthroughs.body_html:
Most religions reject the use of nuclear weapons.

They fail just war: they cannot discriminate (civilians die) and they are disproportionate.

Some Christians and Muslims accept deterrence — possessing weapons to prevent attack — though Pope Francis condemned even possession in 2017. Quakers reject all WMD.

Terrorism uses violence against civilians to spread fear.

It is condemned by mainstream Christianity and Islam: it fails just war (no legitimate authority, no discrimination), and the Qur'an forbids killing innocents (5:32).

'Whoever kills a soul. it is as if he had slain mankind entirely.' — Qur'an 5:32.

A conscientious objector refuses military service for moral or religious reasons.

In WW1 and WW2 many Quakers refused to fight, instead serving in ambulance units. Some were imprisoned.

Dietrich Bonhoeffer was a Christian pacifist who came to resist Hitler. Pope John Paul II spoke against the 2003 Iraq War. Reconciliation — like South Africa's Truth & Reconciliation Commission — aims to heal after conflict.

mcqs.q: Why do most religious thinkers reject nuclear weapons?
options: They cannot discriminate and are disproportionate

mcqs.q: A conscientious objector is someone who:
options: Refuses military service for moral reasons
